items.q: What is an .xlsx file, as openpyxl reads it?
options: A zip archive of XML parts
A binary dump of Excel's memory
A text file of comma-separated values
rationales: The file is a zip archive; a saved workbook lists members such as xl/workbook.xml and xl/styles.xml.
A CSV file holds no sheets, fonts or formulas; an .xlsx file is a zip archive of XML parts.

items.q: A new workbook is made with wb = openpyxl.Workbook(). What is wb.sheetnames before anything else is done?
rationales: A new workbook already has one sheet, so the list is not empty.
The first sheet of a new workbook is named Sheet; Sheet1 is the name Excel gives.
Column letters do not carry a number; after Z the names are AA, AB and so on.
AB is column 28.
The row comes first in the call, so row 3 and column 2 is B3, not C2.
That would be row 2.
Column 26 is Z; AA follows it.
52 is the index of AZ, not AA.

items.q: After wb = openpyxl.Workbook() and wb.create_sheet(index=0, title='First'), what is wb.sheetnames?
rationales: The index 0 puts the new sheet first.
The new workbook's own sheet named Sheet is still there.

items.q: Font(size=24, italic=True) is made and assigned to a cell. What is the name attribute of that Font object?
rationales: That name appears only when it is passed to Font.
A new cell's own font is Calibri, but a Font made with other keywords has no name.

items.q: A formula =SUM(A1:A2) is written with openpyxl and the file is never opened in Excel. What does load_workbook(file, data_only=True).active['A3'].value give?
rationales: No spreadsheet application has calculated it, so there is no stored value and openpyxl does not calculate.
That is what loading without data_only gives.

items.q: What does sheet.freeze_panes = 'C2' keep in view while the sheet scrolls?
options: Row 1 and columns A and B
rationales: The cell itself is not frozen: the rows above it and the columns to its left are.
Columns to the left are frozen as well.
That reads the integers as row first; the documented order is min_col, min_row, max_col, max_row.
The columns are right but the rows are 3 to 5.

items.q: After sheet.merge_cells('A1:D3'), what happens on sheet['B2'] = 'x'?
options: An AttributeError is raised, because B2 is a read-only MergedCell
The merged cell's text becomes x
x is stored in B2 and A1 keeps its text
rationales: Only the top-left cell holds the value of a merged area.
A cell inside a merged area cannot be written to.

items.q: Some code reads sheet['A100'].value on a sheet whose data ends at row 7. Why does range(2, sheet.max_row + 1) then reach row 100?
options: Reading a cell creates it, so max_row becomes 100
max_row is fixed when the file is loaded
range() always runs to the last row Excel allows
rationales: In the run, max_row grew to 100 after only a read.
range() stops at the number it is given; max_row decides that number.
